meta.what: Round 6 C6: more evidence for the no-war counterfactual of each country's trade with Ukraine (buy_ukr = goods bought from Ukraine, sell_ukr = goods sold to Ukraine). Replaces the buy_ukr and sell_ukr entries of counterfactual.json (round 4); other flows there are unchanged.
meta.units: multiplier_vs_2021: real level relative to 2021 (2026 = annual rate, as in counterfactual.json); eur_bn_at_2018_2021_prices: EUR bn, 2021 level revalued at the flow's 2018-2021 average price x multiplier; cumulative_band: multiplier on the SUM over H years of the central expected level (as cf_bands.json). Gains: 1 - median absolute log error of the model / that of the random walk.
meta.method: Three new kinds of evidence, all with the round-4 code, data and decision rule. (1) Rolling origins: last data years L = 2004-2012 (targets up to 2013; 2014+ is war-affected for Ukraine flows) and L = 2016-2019 (targets up to 2021 without 2020). Fitted models are trained only on year pairs ending by L, so they exist from L = 2007 (2006 has 369 pairs of horizon 1 and is not used). (2) Analogues: every country's trade with Poland, Romania, Türkiye, Kazakhstan, Georgia, Moldova, Bulgaria and Hungary (IMF DOTS), L = 2007-2019, targets to 2021 without 2020, models trained on the Russia/Ukraine pairs only. (3) Ukraine-side controls that are not war outcomes: the IMF WEO forecast of Ukraine's real GDP made at the origin (October of L; April 2011 and April 2008 where October is missing) and an index of Ukraine's export prices (cereals 0.33, sunflower/vegetable oil 0.17, iron ore 0.17, steel 0.33) from the WEO commodity paths at the origin. Commodity features of the fitted models are also scored with the WEO path at the origin ('_fc'), because production uses the October 2021 WEO path, not realised prices; the round-4 back-test used realised prices.
meta.decision_rule: As round 4: the eligible model with the lowest mean error is used only if it beats the random walk by >= 15% in every test, or by >= 15% on average with no test worse; otherwise the random walk. Here every origin is a test. Eligible = inputs available in production without war outcomes (rule-based share/GDP/volume models and the _fc variants; not the realised-price or oracle variants).

models.sh_last: year-L share of the country's same-direction trade with the rest of the world, x realised rest-of-world trade
models.vol: level x realised import/export volume growth
models.lin / rf / gbm: round-4 pooled Huber linear / random forest / boosted trees, realised commodity prices in the test (as in round 4)
models.lin_fc / rf_fc / gbm_fc: the same fitted models, commodity features from the WEO path at the origin (as production)
models.lin_g_fc / rf_g_fc: + the WEO forecast of Ukraine (analogue: the partner) real GDP growth made at the origin
models.lin_ua_fc / rf_ua_fc: + that GDP forecast and the Ukraine export-price index from the WEO paths at the origin
models.lin_ua_oracle / rf_ua_oracle: the same with realised Ukraine GDP and prices (not usable; shows the ceiling)

buy_ukr.why: No production-usable model beats the random walk by 15% on Ukraine's own history: best mean gain over the 10 fitted origins is +8.8% (rf_ua_fc), +8.5% (lin_g_fc), +7.8% (vol), +6.9% (sh_last); the round-4 lin with production price inputs (lin_fc) gains +4.3% on average with 2 of 10 origins worse (down to -16%). The models do help a little (pooled +8-13%, bootstrap intervals above zero) but far below the bar.

sell_ukr.why: Strictly, nothing passes: sh_last gains +20% on average over 13 origins (+18% over the 10 fitted origins) but is 0.8% worse at L = 2008; lin_ua_fc gains +24% but is 18% worse at L = 2011. Without the 2013 targets (Russia's 2013 trade blockade of Ukraine and the Euromaidan) both pass. The round-4 rf with production price inputs (rf_fc) gains only +5.8% with 4 of 10 origins worse (down to -34%). sh_last is the only model never materially worse on Ukraine's history and on all 13 analogue origins (min +5%); it is given per country as alternative_sh_last if the owner accepts the 0.8% tie.

IMF World Economic Outlook vintages April 2008 - October 2021 (real GDP growth NGDP_RPCH; commodity price paths PCEREW, PVOILW, PMETAW, PNFUELW, PNRGW, POILAPSP), via DBnomics
IMF Direction of Trade Statistics, annual, imports c.i.f. and exports f.o.b. by partner, via DBnomics

World Bank WDI real GDP (realised Ukraine GDP for the oracle variant and for training)

overlaps: None in money: this file moves no euros by itself; it replaces the expected (no-war) level of buy_ukr and sell_ukr in counterfactual.json. The builder must use these entries INSTEAD of the counterfactual.json buy_ukr/sell_ukr entries, never on top. cf_bands.json (B1) gives generic cumulative bands per model and size class computed on the round-4 errors (lin for buy_ukr, rf for sell_ukr); for these two flows the per-country cumulative_band here (random walk, rolling-origin errors) should be used, and since obj.cf becomes 'rw' the generic fallback would anyway pick cf_bands' rw cells. cf_bands.json has no per-country buy_ukr/sell_ukr entries, so nothing else collides. Trade levels themselves (trade_full.json) are untouched.
notes: The round-4 back-test scored lin and rf with realised commodity prices, while production feeds them the October 2021 WEO path. With the origin's WEO path, their gains for Ukraine flows roughly halve (pooled over the 10 origins: buy_ukr lin +13% -> +8%, rf +13% -> +8%; sell_ukr lin +22% -> +6%, rf +18% -> +10%). On the two round-4 tests alone the round-4 choices still pass with production inputs (buy_ukr lin_fc +15.5%, sell_ukr rf_fc +22.8%), so round 4 was not wrong on its evidence; the rolling origins show those two tests were favourable.

Ukraine-side controls: the WEO forecast of Ukraine GDP helps sell_ukr (what partners sell to Ukraine follows Ukraine's demand): pooled gain +25-28% vs +6% without, mostly from the 2016-2019 origins when the forecasts were right; it hurts at 2011-2012, when the WEO expected 4-5% growth and Ukraine stagnated. For buy_ukr it helps only slightly (lin_g_fc +8.5% vs lin_fc +4.3% mean over origins). The export-price index adds little on top of it. The October 2021 WEO expected 3.4-4.0% a year for Ukraine in 2022-2026 (+17% in logs by 2026); with the fitted coefficient of about 1.9, the GDP term alone would lift the no-war level of sales to Ukraine by about x1.4 by 2026 on one forecast, which is too fragile given the 2011-2012 failure.

Analogues: for Poland, Romania, Türkiye, Bulgaria and Hungary as partners the share model and the partner-GDP nowcast beat the random walk by 12-38% on average; for Kazakhstan and Georgia (commodity- and shock-driven partners like Ukraine) no model beats it on average. The model class works for steady partners and not for volatile ones; Ukraine's own history places it with the volatile group for buy_ukr.

The random walk is biased low for trade with Ukraine (median actual above the 2021 level by +0.2-0.3 log after five years in growth periods). The yearly and cumulative bands are asymmetric and carry this (cumulative median ratio x1.2 over 2022-2026), but the central stays at the 2021 level as the rule requires.

Era hold-out coverage (quantiles from 2004-2012 scored on 2016-2019 and the reverse): yearly 92%/83% (buy_ukr rw), 97%/69% (sell_ukr rw), 95%/78% (sell_ukr sh_last). The 2008-2009 collapse of Ukraine's imports (and the end of Turkmen gas sales in 2009) is not predictable from the 2016-2019 era. The bands pool both eras, so they include such shocks once.
Hubs (ARM GEO KAZ KGZ UZB TUR AZE MNG TJK SRB ARE) and Belarus keep the random walk in the alternative too.
2026 is January-August; multipliers are annual rates as in counterfactual.json.
